questions.prompt: The motion of a particle is defined by the relation $x = 6t^4 - 2t^3 - 12t^2 + 3t + 3$, where $x$ and $t$ are expressed in meters and seconds, respectively. Determine the **velocity** of the particle at the instant when $a = 0$ (in $\text{m/s}$).

The motion of a particle is defined by the relation $x = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 4$, where $x$ is expressed in meters and $t$ in seconds. Determine the **total distance traveled** by the particle from $t = 0$ to the instant when the acceleration is zero (in $\text{m}$).
The motion of a particle is defined by $x = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 24t + 4$ ($x$ in meters, $t$ in seconds). At what times is the velocity zero?

The acceleration of a particle is defined by the relation $a = -0.8v$, where $a$ is in $\text{m/s}^2$ and $v$ in $\text{m/s}$. Knowing that at $t = 0$ the velocity is $1\,\text{m/s}$, determine the time required for the velocity to be reduced by 50 percent of its initial value (in $\text{s}$).
questions.solution:
Class $a = f(v)$: $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -0.8v \Rightarrow \displaystyle\int_1^{v}\frac{dv}{v} = -0.8\int_0^t dt \Rightarrow \ln v = -0.8t$.

For $v = 0.5\,\text{m/s}$: $t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{0.8} = 0.866\,\text{s}$.

(For the stopping distance, $v\,dv/dx = -0.8v$ gives $v = 1 - 0.8x$, so the particle stops after $1.250\,\text{m}$.)

questions.prompt: The acceleration of a particle is defined by $a = -k\sqrt{v}$, where $k$ is a constant. Knowing that $x = 0$ and $v = 81\,\text{m/s}$ at $t = 0$ and that $v = 36\,\text{m/s}$ when $x = 18\,\text{m}$, determine the velocity of the particle when $x = 20\,\text{m}$ (in $\text{m/s}$).
questions.solution:
Use $a = v\,dv/dx$: $v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -k v^{1/2} \Rightarrow v^{1/2}dv = -k\,dx \Rightarrow \tfrac23\big(v^{3/2} - 81^{3/2}\big) = -kx$.

With $v = 36$ at $x = 18$: $\tfrac23(216 - 729) = -18k \Rightarrow k = 19\,\text{m}^{1/2}\text{s}^{-3/2}$.

At $x = 20\,\text{m}$: $v^{3/2} = 729 - \tfrac32(19)(20) = 159 \Rightarrow v = 159^{2/3} = 29.3\,\text{m/s}$.

questions.prompt: A particle is projected to the right from $x = 0$ with an initial velocity of $9\,\text{m/s}$. Its acceleration is $a = -0.6v^{3/2}$ ($a$ in $\text{m/s}^2$, $v$ in $\text{m/s}$). Determine the distance the particle will have traveled when its velocity is $4\,\text{m/s}$ (in $\text{m}$).

A stone is thrown vertically upward from a point on a bridge located $40\,\text{m}$ above the water. Knowing that it strikes the water $4\,\text{s}$ after release, determine the speed with which the stone strikes the water (in $\text{m/s}$).
questions.solution:
Origin at the water, $y$ positive upward: $y_0 = 40\,\text{m}$, $a = -9.81\,\text{m/s}^2$.

$y = y_0 + v_0t + \tfrac12at^2$: $0 = 40 + 4v_0 - 4.905(16) \Rightarrow v_0 = \dfrac{78.48 - 40}{4} = 9.62\,\text{m/s}\uparrow$.

$v = v_0 + at = 9.62 - 9.81(4) = -29.6\,\text{m/s}$, so the stone strikes the water at $29.6\,\text{m/s}\downarrow$.

questions.prompt: A motorist is traveling at $54\,\text{km/h}$ when she observes that a traffic light $240\,\text{m}$ ahead turns red. The light stays red for $24\,\text{s}$. If she wishes to pass the light without stopping just as it turns green, determine the **magnitude** of the required uniform deceleration (in $\text{m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
$v_0 = 54\,\text{km/h} = 15\,\text{m/s}$. Uniformly accelerated motion with $x - x_0 = 240\,\text{m}$ at $t = 24\,\text{s}$:

$240 = 15(24) + \tfrac12a(24)^2 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{240 - 360}{288} = -0.417\,\text{m/s}^2$.

Deceleration magnitude $0.417\,\text{m/s}^2$. (Speed at the light: $v = 15 - 0.417(24) = 5\,\text{m/s} = 18.00\,\text{km/h}$.)

questions.prompt: In a boat race, boat $A$ is leading boat $B$ by $50\,\text{m}$ and both boats are traveling at a constant speed of $180\,\text{km/h}$. At $t = 0$, the boats accelerate at constant rates. Knowing that when $B$ passes $A$, $t = 8\,\text{s}$ and $v_A = 225\,\text{km/h}$, determine the acceleration of boat $B$ (in $\text{m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
$180\,\text{km/h} = 50\,\text{m/s}$, $225\,\text{km/h} = 62.5\,\text{m/s}$. Origin at $B$'s initial position.

Boat $A$: $a_A = \dfrac{62.5 - 50}{8} = 1.5625\,\text{m/s}^2$; $x_A = 50 + 50(8) + \tfrac12(1.5625)(8)^2 = 500\,\text{m}$.

Boat $B$ passes $A$, so $x_B = x_A$: $500 = 0 + 50(8) + \tfrac12a_B(64) \Rightarrow a_B = \dfrac{100}{32} = 3.13\,\text{m/s}^2$.

questions.prompt: An elevator is moving upward at a constant speed of $4\,\text{m/s}$. A man standing $10\,\text{m}$ above the top of the elevator throws a ball upward with a speed of $3\,\text{m/s}$. Determine when the ball will hit the elevator (in $\text{s}$).
questions.solution:
Origin at the initial top of the elevator, $y$ upward. Ball: $y_B = 10 + 3t - 4.905t^2$. Elevator: $y_E = 4t$.

Contact when $y_B = y_E$: $10 + 3t - 4.905t^2 = 4t \Rightarrow 4.905t^2 + t - 10 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{1 + 196.2}}{9.81} = 1.330\,\text{s}$.

(Ball position relative to the man: $3(1.330) - 4.905(1.330)^2 = -4.68\,\text{m}$, i.e. $4.68\,\text{m}$ below the man.)

questions.prompt: A model boat has initial horizontal velocity $6\,\text{m/s}$; its acceleration varies linearly from $-12\,\text{m/s}^2$ at $t = 0$ to $-2\,\text{m/s}^2$ at $t = t_1$, then remains $-2\,\text{m/s}^2$ until $t = 1.4\,\text{s}$. Knowing that $v = 1.8\,\text{m/s}$ when $t = t_1$, determine the position of the model at $t = 1.4\,\text{s}$ (in $\text{m}$, starting from $x = 0$).

A ball is thrown so that the motion is defined by $x = 5t$ and $y = 2 + 6t - 4.9t^2$ ($x$, $y$ in meters, $t$ in seconds). Determine the horizontal distance the ball travels before hitting the ground (in $\text{m}$).
questions.solution:
Ground: $y = 0 \Rightarrow 4.9t^2 - 6t - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{36 + 39.2}}{9.8} = 1.497\,\text{s}$.

$x = 5(1.497) = 7.49\,\text{m}$.

(At $t = 1\,\text{s}$: $v_x = 5$, $v_y = 6 - 9.8 = -3.8\,\text{m/s}$, $v = 6.28\,\text{m/s}$ at $37.2^\circ$ below the horizontal.)

questions.prompt: A helicopter is flying with a constant horizontal velocity of $180\,\text{km/h}$ and is directly above point $A$ when a loose part begins to fall. The part lands $6.5\,\text{s}$ later at point $B$ on the surface inclined at $10^\circ$ as shown. Determine the distance $d$ between points $A$ and $B$ (in $\text{m}$).
questions.solution:
The part keeps the helicopter's horizontal velocity, $(v_x)_0 = 180\,\text{km/h} = 50\,\text{m/s}$, and $(v_y)_0 = 0$.

Horizontal (uniform): $x = 50(6.5) = 325\,\text{m}$.

$B$ lies on the $10^\circ$ incline through $A$, so $d = \dfrac{x}{\cos 10^\circ} = \dfrac{325}{0.9848} = 330\,\text{m}$.

(Vertical drop $= \tfrac12(9.81)(6.5)^2 = 207.2\,\text{m} = h + 325\tan 10^\circ$, giving $h = 149.9\,\text{m}$.)

questions.prompt: During a rainstorm the paths of the raindrops appear to form an angle of $30^\circ$ with the vertical and to be directed to the left when observed from a side window of a train moving at $15\,\text{km/h}$. When the train's speed has increased to $24\,\text{km/h}$, the angle appears to be $45^\circ$. If the train were stopped, with what speed would the drops be observed to fall (in $\text{m/s}$)?
questions.solution:
Let the drop velocity be $v_x$ (to the right, direction of the train) and $v_y\downarrow$. Relative to the train, $\mathbf{v}_{D/T} = \mathbf{v}_D - \mathbf{v}_T$ has horizontal component $v_T - v_x$ to the left and vertical component $v_y$.

$15\,\text{km/h} = 4.167\,\text{m/s}$: $4.167 - v_x = v_y\tan 30^\circ$.
$24\,\text{km/h} = 6.667\,\text{m/s}$: $6.667 - v_x = v_y\tan 45^\circ$.

Subtracting: $2.5 = v_y(1 - 0.5774) \Rightarrow v_y = 5.915\,\text{m/s}$; then $v_x = 6.667 - 5.915 = 0.752\,\text{m/s}$.

$v = \sqrt{0.752^2 + 5.915^2} = 5.96\,\text{m/s}$, at $\tan^{-1}(5.915/0.752) = 82.8^\circ$ with the horizontal.

questions.prompt: Determine the smallest radius that should be used for a highway if the normal component of the acceleration of a car traveling at $72\,\text{km/h}$ is not to exceed $0.8\,\text{m/s}^2$ (in $\text{m}$).

Determine the maximum speed that the cars of a roller-coaster can reach along a circular portion of track of radius $\rho = 25\,\text{m}$ if the normal component of their acceleration cannot exceed $3g$.
questions.solution:
$a_n = v^2/\rho \le 3g \Rightarrow v_{\max} = \sqrt{3g\rho} = \sqrt{3(9.81)(25)} = 27.1\,\text{m/s} = 27.1(3.6) = 97.6\,\text{km/h}$.

Option A uses $g$ instead of $3g$; option B forgets to convert m/s to km/h; option D applies the factor 3 outside the square root.
